study.title: RPD: Learning Efficient Crops and Weeds for Field Semantic Segmentation in Drone Images
study.short_title: Drone crop/weed: RPD-Net mIoU 0.8747, 0.14M params, 7 FPS Jetson TX2
study.venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing

segmentation.domain: Crop/weed semantic segmentation in drone imagery for precision agriculture (vision-based field management, site-specific spraying); lightweight reparameterized pixel difference (RPD) network robust to natural illumination variation
segmentation.best_model: RPD-Net (theta=0.5) on PhenoBench validation: mIoU 88.26 ± 0.77 (max); headline RPD-Net (theta=1) 87.47 ± 0.75 with only 38% of ERFNet's parameters and fewer MACs (13.45G vs 33.05G). D-RPD-Net 87.54 ± 0.67. All variants exceed 70 weed IoU. Trained from scratch

dataset.name: PhenoBench (primary; sugarbeet, drone-acquired per the paper, ~21 m flight height, GSD 1 mm/px, multi-date illumination subsets Sunny I/Sunny II/Overcast, eval 1024x1024) plus CoFly-WeedDB (cotton, 5 m flight height, ~1.4-1.6 mm/px, 3 weed species + background)
dataset.note: Paper explicitly states PhenoBench images were 'captured by a drone equipped with a high-resolution camera at a flight height of approximately 21 m, corresponding to a GSD of 1 mm/pixel'; flag: the original PhenoBench release (Weyler et al. 2024) describes close-range field-robot acquisition, so the platform description here may differ from the source dataset. CoFly flown at 5 m. Image count 2872 from the original PhenoBench, not restated in this text.

segmentation.backbone: Lightweight encoder-decoder built on reparameterized pixel difference (RPD) blocks: parallel depthwise PDC operators (central/angular/radial CPDC, APDC, RPDC) + pointwise fusion with skip connections; max-pool downsampling / bilinear upsampling (no learnable params); ReLU; structural + weight reparameterization collapses multi-branch training form to single-path inference. 0.189M params/MACs 13.45G before rep; 0.14M params/4.71G MACs after @768x768. Trained from scratch, weighted CE loss, Adam, 4096 epochs, batch 4

mIoU.quote: RPD-Net achieves an mIoU of 87.47(±0.75), higher than the lightweight ERFNet (85.19) while using only 38% of its parameters ... The variants RPD-Net (θ = 0.5) and D-RPD-Net reach mIoU of 88.26(±0.77) and 87.54(±0.67), respectively
mIoU.ambiguity: PhenoBench validation set, mean over 5 random seeds (+/- std). Headline RPD-Net (theta=1) 0.8747; best variant theta=0.5 0.8826; D-RPD-Net 0.8754; ERFNet 0.8519. All variants exceed 0.70 weed IoU (e.g., 0.7653 vs SegFormer-B0 0.6801 under Overcast). Statistical significance via paired t-test (t=7.13, p=0.0021 vs SegFormer-B0). Ablation training-set mIoU up to 0.9077 (complete RPD 'CAR').

mPA.ambiguity: Mean/backbone pixel accuracy not reported in extracted text.

F1.quote: Table VI ... 'MP,' 'MR,' and 'MF1' denote Macro Precision, Recall, and F1-Score
F1.ambiguity: Macro and per-class F1 are reported in Table VI (P/R/F1 per class) but numeric values are not present in the extracted text (table rendered as image); only IoU/latency numbers are obtainable.

PA.ambiguity: Micro accuracy (MACC) reported in Table VI but numeric values not present in extracted text; per-class true-positive rates in Sunny I confusion matrices (soil 0.9973, crop 0.9803, weed 0.8468) are TP rates, not PA.

weed_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 exists in Table VI but values not extractable; weed reported as IoU (above 0.70 for all RPD variants; 0.7653 vs SegFormer-B0 0.6801 Overcast; 0.5311 Sunny I).

crop_F1.ambiguity: Per-class F1 exists in Table VI but values not extractable; crop reported as IoU only.

edge.device: NVIDIA Jetson TX2 (Tegra, embedded); comparison hardware: NVIDIA RTX 3090 (x2, evaluation on single GPU) and CPU
edge.framework: PyTorch (training); TensorRT evaluation on Jetson (TensorRT does not support the bilinear interpolation used in RPD-Net, slight slowdown vs ERFNet; no extra Jetson optimization explored)

fps.quote: The 42.05 frames/s on RTX 3090 and the 7.0 fps on Jetson provide a promising reference for eﬃcient inference in agricultural applications
fps.ambiguity: edge.reported=true: on-device Jetson TX2 measurement (forward pass, 5-run averages). Input resolution (512/768/1024 tested) not tied to the 7.0 fps figure in text. Contrast: 42.05 fps on RTX 3090 (1000/23.8ms).

latency_ms.quote: the 7.0 fps on Jetson ... our method attains a latency of 23.8 ms
latency_ms.ambiguity: 142.9 ms is derived as 1000/7.0 on Jetson TX2 (EDGE, fps figure resolution-unspecified). Paper-reported 23.8 ms is the RTX 3090 per-frame inference latency (Table V, ~42 fps) - reported there, not on edge hardware.

power_w.quote: RPD-Net exhibits slightly lower power usage and stable thermal behavior relative to other baselines. After reparameterization, power consumption shows a modest decrease
power_w.ambiguity: Table XI reports power (W/frame = average device power / achieved fps) and onboard thermal temperature on Jetson TX2, 5-run averages, but numeric values are not present in the extracted text (table rendered as image); only the qualitative 'slightly lower + stable' statement is available. Duplicate of the same qualitative claim in Section IV-B.

params_M.quote: After reparameterization, the parameter counts of RPD-Net decrease from 0.189M to 0.14M
params_M.ambiguity: Structural computational metric. 0.14M is the inference-time (reparameterized) form used on-device; training-form is 0.189M. CoFly binary config also 0.189M / 0.52G MACs.

gflops.quote: the MACs reduce from 13.45G to 4.71G at a 768 × 768 input resolution
gflops.ambiguity: DERIVED: 9.42 GFLOPs = 2 x 4.71G MACs (post-reparameterization inference form) at 768x768 input. Paper reports MACs, not FLOPs. Training-form 13.45G MACs (26.9 GFLOPs). Input-resolution dependent.

issues: edge.reported=true: genuine on-device Jetson TX2 measurement (7.0 FPS; power W/frame + thermal profiling in Table XI); no extra Jetson optimization and TensorRT lacks bilinear-interpolation support (notes a slower-than-ERFNet case on Jetson). 23.8 ms / 42.05 fps figures are RTX 3090 (desktop).

PhenoBench described in-paper as drone-acquired (~21 m, 1 mm/px); the original PhenoBench release (Weyler et al. 2024) documents close-range field-robot acquisition - platform description flagged as possibly differing from the source dataset. uav_collected=true reflects the paper's explicit claim.

Table VI (macro + per-class P/R/F1, MACC) and Table XI (Jetson W/frame, temperature) are image-rendered; their numeric values are unavailable in the extracted text, so only IoU/latency/params/MACs numbers are captured.

Headline results on PhenoBench validation: RPD-Net (theta=1) 87.47 mIoU, best variant theta=0.5 88.26, D-RPD-Net 87.54, all exceeding 0.70 weed IoU; statistically significant vs lightweight baselines (paired t-test p<0.05).

Reparameterization is the efficiency core: params 0.189M->0.14M, MACs 13.45G->4.71G (768x768), no accuracy loss; RPD-Net + D-RPD-Net beat ERFNet/EfficientViT/SegFormer/SegNeXt/FG-UNet baselines in the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. Trained from scratch.
Generalization on CoFly (drone, 5 m, cotton): binary weed-vs-background mIoU RPD-Net 0.5989 / D-RPD-Net 0.6084 (weed IoU 0.4206/0.4303); multiclass IoU low for sparse purslane class (2.17).
